CHIEF COMPLAINT
Difficulty swallowing.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Tyler is a 56-year-old male presenting with difficulty swallowing for four to five weeks. He describes a sensation of something stuck in his throat that bothers him intermittently throughout the day, sometimes causing mild pain. He reports that solid foods are particularly problematic while liquids pass without difficulty. He occasionally needs liquid to help wash down solid foods. He denies ever choking completely but acknowledges worry about potential choking. He denies change in symptoms with temperature of food or liquid. He denies hemoptysis, hematemesis, or vomiting. He denies weight loss. He denies associated chest pain or shortness of breath.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or medication side effects.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Diabetes mellitus
Hypertension

MEDICATIONS
Metformin 500 mg twice daily
Norvasc

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Neck: No swelling. Thyroid normal without masses. No lymphadenopathy.
Oropharynx: No masses, swelling, or redness.
Cardiovascular: No carotid bruits. Heart exam normal without murmurs.
Pulmonary: Lungs clear.
Abdomen: Epigastric tenderness to palpation. No masses or significant swelling.
Back: Normal.
Extremities: Normal.
Neurological: Fine.

RESULTS
Hemoglobin A1c: 7.4 (previously obtained)
Home blood glucose monitoring: Patient reports checking approximately 80% of the time, with values in target range.
Home blood pressure: Patient reports values usually close to or within target range.
In-office blood pressure: 120/50 mmHg

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Dysphagia: Concern for esophageal stricture or narrowing. Referral to gastroenterology for endoscopic evaluation. Started Prilosec 20 mg once daily. Patient instructed to chew foods thoroughly, especially hard foods. Advised to seek emergency care if food becomes impacted. Instructed to call office if symptoms worsen.

Diabetes mellitus: Repeat hemoglobin A1c ordered. Laboratory work ordered including kidney function tests. Referral to ophthalmology for evaluation of diabetic retinopathy. Continue metformin. Follow-up in approximately one month to review results and adjust medications if needed.

Hypertension: Well-controlled on current therapy. Continue Norvasc. Refill sent to pharmacy.
